newsitem.title: UK: Laura Ashley sees H1 loss, breakeven year.
newsitem.headline: Laura Ashley sees H1 loss, breakeven year.

text.p: British retailer Laura Ashley Holdings Plc, hit by losses in the U.S., said on Tuesday it expected to report a first-half pretax loss of about 4.5 million pounds ($7.2 million), including a charge for closing two Welsh plants.
Laura Ashley said it expected to return to profit in the current half, resulting in approximately breakeven full-year pretax figures.

The company, which last issued a profit warning in April, said it would take a first-half charge of about one million pounds to close two loss-making garment sewing factories at Caernarfon and Machynlleth in Wales.
About 190 jobs would be cut as a result of the closures, the company said in a statement.
The company's shares, hit in recent months by management changes and profit warnings, firmed 1.5 pence to 58 by 0745 GMT.
Laura Ashley said its second-half pretax results would be lower-than-expected due to slower sales, particularly in the U.S., and a two million pound U.S. advertising campaign.
The company planned to curtail the opening of more U.S. stores until new store performance improved.
Laura Ashley said U.S. losses would not be offset fully by profits generated in the UK, Japan and Germany.

Total like-for-like sales rose 11 percent in the 26 weeks to July 26, while the company's half-year stock position was 76.8 million pounds, down from 93.1 million at end-January. ($ = 0.622 British Pounds)
